title: Frontend: Fibonacci Modulo (Pisano Period)
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Fibonacci Modulo (Pisano Period). This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({n,modulus}), with nonnegative decimal-string n and positive integer modulus <= 1000000. Return F_n modulo modulus as a number. Use modular fast doubling so a huge index does not require period discovery. Invalid inputs throw Invalid input.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
A Pisano period is the repetition length of the pair (F_n mod m,F_(n+1) mod m).
alternativeApproaches: Use fast doubling as the general method and explain when explicit period discovery is useful or wasteful.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: m=1; n=0; small known cycle.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
